title: Association of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors With the Risk for Spontaneous Intracranial Hemorrhage
authors: Renoux C, Vahey S, Dell'Aniello S, Boivin JF
population: New users of antidepressants aged 18 or older in more than 650 UK general practices of the Clinical Practice Research Datalink; nested case-control analysis of 3036 intracranial haemorrhages and 89,702 matched controls
funder: This study was supported by operating grant MOP-133553 from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research and a Chercheur-Boursier Award from the Fonds de la Recherche en Santé du Québec. The funding sources had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
result: Overall incidence of intracranial haemorrhage 3.8 per 10,000 person-years. Current SSRI use against tricyclic use: RR 1.17 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.35), an absolute excess of 6.7 (0.2 to 13.2) per 100,000 person-years; first 30 days RR 1.44 (1.04 to 1.99). Strong against weak serotonin reuptake inhibitors RR 1.25 (1.01 to 1.54), excess 9.5 per 100,000 person-years; among users of oral anticoagulants RR 3.08 (0.89 to 10.63) with sampled controls and 1.73 (0.89 to 3.39) with all controls, neither statistically significant. Against non-use, SSRIs RR 1.35 (1.22 to 1.50).
